name: Should I remodel the front yard with the house exterior?

mainEntity.name: Should front yard hardscape and landscaping be included in the same exterior remodel as the house façade?
mainEntity.text: Should front yard hardscape and landscaping be included in the same exterior remodel as the house façade?

acceptedAnswer.text: Front yard hardscape and landscaping are often strongest when they are planned with the house exterior instead of as a separate afterthought. The driveway, walkway, planting beds, lighting, and entry path all influence how the façade is perceived, and they can also affect drainage and access. When these elements are coordinated together, the final result usually looks more intentional and higher end. It also allows the contractor to align grades, transitions, and material colors so the front elevation and yard feel like one design. That said, not every project needs to include everything at once. If the budget is tight, it may be better to complete the building shell first and phase the yard later. The key is to think about how water flows, where people walk, and how the front of the property reads from the street. A well-planned front yard can make a significant difference in the impact of an exterior remodel, especially in neighborhoods where curb appeal drives value.
acceptedAnswer.description: Yes, front yard hardscape and landscaping are often worth including because they shape curb appeal, drainage, and the overall design. Coordinating the yard with the façade prevents mismatched materials and lets the entry, walkways, lighting, and planting work together. The main exception is when budget or permits make it smarter to stage the work.
